summary: ui-pages review of src/ui/pages/** (10.4k LOC, 11 files). I read every production section in full (live, mixer, inventory, stats, graph, settings, settings/connections, doctor, help) and skimmed the test modules. Skills applied: frontend-ui-engineering, frontend-dev-guidelines (its React/MUI stack does not apply here; only the principles carried over), code-perfection and refactoring-guru. Five problems dominate: (1) the page boundary leaks; (2) domain policy lives in GTK files; (3) four god files mix view, presenter, controller and IO; (4) copy-paste across pages; (5) concrete defects (unescaped StatusPage markup, name-based DFS widget lookup with unwraps, per-frame tick callbacks and 100 ms polling, SpinRow writing config on every step). Splits move pure logic first, then each page becomes a <page>/ directory, then NavigationContext.state becomes private with an architecture test. Caveats: inventory.rs has an include_str!("inventory.rs") self-scan test; native tests must run through python3 tools/test-native.py; reviewer ran no tests; a11y tooltip-as-name claims marked PLAUSIBLE. || VERIFIER: 10 confirmed, 14 adjusted, 1 refuted of 25 findings; splits: 1 confirmed, 6 adjusted. Key corrections: NavigationContext.state is used by ~40 non-page ui files, so privatizing it is a separate epic (scope the architecture test to ui/pages); domain cannot import storage and SceneRegistrySnapshot lacks order/filter/favorite, so deck projection needs a new domain input; inventory does not share the live-switchable slot list; ui-pages-17 refuted (config writes already coalesce via run_config_snapshot, and debounce is explicitly rejected in its doc); keep eprintln for SCENEDECK_MIXER_INSPECT (manual test plan relies on raw lines); stats vs health disagreement comes from cumulative vs windowed ratios, not constants; inventory reconcile cost is linear not quadratic; include_str test breaks loudly at compile time after git mv. No tests were run by the verifier.

findings.title: NavigationContext exposes the raw Rc<RefCell<AppState>>; pages read and mutate AppState fields directly, contrary to the documented page contract
findings.evidence: `pub(crate) state: Rc<RefCell<AppState>>` (navigation.rs:20). Pages write fields directly: mixer.rs:585-586 `state.mixer.mode = mode`, 631-635 (selected_scene plus the pinned-scene rule), 676 grouping, 705 search, 837 `invalidate_active_audio()`; settings.rs:48 `startup_notice.take()`, 131 `set_theme_mode`, 781-783 `update(&mut state.config.outputs, active)`; connections.rs:121, 146, 156, 249 `obs_password = ...`; doctor.rs:107 `begin_topology_refresh(&mut nav.state.borrow_mut())`. Production line counts: mixer 17 borrow_mut, live 9, stats 7, connections 7; inventory 16 state.borrow. CLAUDE.md says pages expose only switch_to_page/dispatch. architecture_tests.rs:647-661 only checks the token `AppController`, so nothing enforces the contract.
findings.recommendation: 1) Add intent methods on AppState in src/controller/state/mixer.rs: `select_mixer_mode(MixerMode)`, `select_mixer_scene(SceneId)` (owns the pinned rule now at mixer.rs:633), `set_mixer_grouping`, `set_mixer_search(&str)`. In src/controller/state.rs add `set_output_confirmation(OutputKind, OutputAction, bool)`. 2) Add `NavigationContext::read<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&AppState)->R)->R` and `update<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut AppState)->R)->R`. 3) Migrate one page per PR. 4) Make `state` private (crate-visible only to ui/window.rs and ui/event_pump.rs) and add architecture test `pages_do_not_borrow_app_state_mutably` grepping src/ui/pages/** production code for `.state.borrow_mut()`.
findings.risk: 559 borrow_mut sites crate-wide make re-entrancy panics possible when a signal fires during a build. The page layer cannot be reasoned about separately from the controller state.
findings.verifier_note: Evidence confirmed: navigation.rs:20 `pub(crate) state`; mixer.rs:585-586, 631-635, 676, 705, 837; settings.rs:48, 781-783; connections.rs:121/146/156/249; doctor.rs:107. Counts re-measured on production sections: mixer 17 borrow_mut, live 9, stats 7, connections 7 (match); inventory has 3 borrow_mut + 10 `state.borrow()` (not 16). settings.rs:131 already calls an AppState intent method (set_theme_mode), so it is not a direct field write. Step 4 is infeasible as written: `nav.state` is read by ~40 non-page files under src/ui (widgets/*, hotkeys.rs, persist.rs, preflight*, sidebar.rs, command_palette.rs, quick_actions.rs, action_catalog.rs, ...), so privatizing the field to window.rs/event_pump.rs breaks the crate. Adjusted step 4: add `NavigationContext::read/update` first, migrate pages, then add architecture test `pages_do_not_borrow_app_state_mutably` scoped to `ui/pages` only (via `violations("ui/pages", &[".state.borrow_mut()"], &[])` — check the scanner handles method-call tokens, it matches substrings per line). Making the field private is a separate, later epic covering all of src/ui. Also note CLAUDE.md text ('exposing only switch_to_page() and dispatch()') is already inaccurate; update the doc in the same PR as the test.

findings.title: Mixer StatusPage descriptions interpolate OBS scene names and error messages without markup escaping
findings.evidence: AdwStatusPage `description` is Pango markup. inventory.rs:340 and graph.rs:81 wrap their text in `glib::markup_escape_text`. Mixer passes `fl!("mixer-error-description", scene, message)` (818-823), `mixer-no-audio-sources-description` with `scene = scene_label` (740-744) and `mixer-loading-description` with `scene` (937) unescaped. A scene named `Q&A` or an error containing `<` fails markup parsing; GTK logs a warning and the description renders empty or garbled.
findings.recommendation: Add `src/ui/widgets/status_page.rs` with `pub(crate) fn status_page(icon:&str, title:&str, literal_description:&str) -> adw::StatusPage` that always calls markup_escape_text and adds `app-status-page`. Replace all 7 StatusPage::builder sites (mixer 398, 799, 815; inventory 337, 362; graph 78, 88). Add a native regression test with scene id `Q&A <b>` mirroring graph.rs:820.
findings.risk: Users see no error text exactly when OBS fails. Translator- or OBS-controlled markup injection is possible.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: mixer.rs:799-806 append_mixer_status passes `description` raw; callers at 736-745 (scene_label) and 933-938 (scene) interpolate OBS scene names; 815-824 interpolates scene + OBS error message. inventory.rs:340 and graph.rs:81 escape. AdwStatusPage description is markup. 7 builder sites in pages, none elsewhere in src/ui. mixer.rs:398 uses only a static Fluent string (low risk) but should still go through the helper. Recommendation sound; Fluent args are inserted with Unicode isolation marks (FSI/PDI) by fluent by default — the regression test should compare after stripping \u{2068}/\u{2069} or check `contains`.

findings.title: inventory.rs is a 2126-line god module: presenter, reconciler, row view, popover editor, drag and drop, YAML dialogs, save-status poller and focus preservation
findings.evidence: InventoryPresentation::read (75-129); build plus reconciler (131-190); update_rows (213-326); populate (330-457); preserve_breakpoint_focus (462-524); build_registry_save_status 100 ms poll (528-572); build_scene_row (598-695); build_role_cell (697-749); build_scene_options (751-892); accent controls (898-952, 1171-1212); install_scene_reordering (960-1010); build_stale_group (1019-1104); reorder logic (1120-1169); YAML import/export (1214-1504). 15 production unwrap/expect.

findings.title: Incremental inventory reconciliation finds widgets by string widget-name through recursive tree walks and unwraps each lookup
findings.evidence: `inventory_widget(container, "inventory-scenes").unwrap().downcast::<gtk4::ListBox>().unwrap()` (222-225); `widget.downcast::<gtk4::ListBoxRow>().unwrap()` (257); role DropDown lookup unwraps (280-283); `options.parent().unwrap().downcast::<GtkBox>().unwrap()` (299-300); `inventory-content` unwrap (312-315). Each lookup is a full DFS (198-211), so one refresh costs O(rows x subtree). A renamed widget panics the GTK main loop.
findings.recommendation: Add `inventory/view.rs`: `struct SceneRowHandle { row, role: DropDown, curation: Label, drag: Image, options_slot: GtkBox }` and `struct InventoryView { list, content, empty, reorder_hint, deck_controls, rows: RefCell<HashMap<SceneId, SceneRowHandle>> }`. build_scene_row returns a SceneRowHandle; update_rows becomes `InventoryView::reconcile(&self, previous, next)` with no name lookups and no unwrap. Guard with native tests at 1766 and 1804.
findings.risk: GTK thread can panic on a structural UI change; refresh cost is quadratic on large scene collections.
findings.verifier_note: Code confirmed at inventory.rs:198-211 (recursive DFS by widget_name) and unwraps at 222-225, 257, 280-283, 297-300, 312-315 (10 unwrap calls on that path). Complexity claim is wrong: per-row lookups search only that row's subtree (`inventory_widget(&row, ...)`), and container-level lookups are a constant count, so one refresh is O(total widget tree), not quadratic. Downgrade the perf part of the risk; the panic-on-restructure risk stands (severity medium-high rather than high). Recommendation (typed SceneRowHandle/InventoryView) is sound; widget names must be kept because native tests use `find(root, name)` (inventory.rs:1872).

findings.title: Scene-registry business rules are implemented inside GTK closures instead of on the registry aggregate
findings.evidence: `registry.retained_scenes.retain(|entry| entry != record)` (1086-1090); `registry.scenes.remove(entry_name).is_some()` (1317); `reordered_scene_ids` and the filter guard in the page (1139-1169) with an `insert_after: bool` flag; stale set computed twice (107-114, 1025-1047); export calls `write_registry_yaml_to_path` directly (1415) while import goes via `ui::persist::import_registry` (1468); page imports storage::registry types (16-18).
findings.recommendation: Add to SceneRegistry: `remove_retained(&RetainedScene)->bool`, `remove_stale_entry(&str)->bool`, `move_scene(inventory_ids, source, target, Placement)->bool` with `enum Placement { Before, After }` and the filter guard inside, `stale_entries(&SceneInventory)->Vec<StaleEntry>`. Coordinate with storage/domain reviewer on moving aggregate behaviour into src/domain/registry.rs. Add `ui::persist::export_registry(nav, path, on_done)`. Move reorder tests (2094-2126) next to SceneRegistry::move_scene.
findings.risk: Invariants like 'no reorder while filtered' can be bypassed by another UI caller; persistence paths differ between import and export.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed: retain at 1086-1090, remove at 1317, filter guard at 1139-1141, reordered_scene_ids 1152-1169 with `insert_after: bool`, stale computed twice (107-114 presentation; 1025-1047 group), export writes via `write_registry_yaml_to_path` at 1414 while import uses persist::import_registry at 1468. Corrections: imports at 16-18 are `parse_scene_accent, scene_accent_hex, write_registry_yaml_to_path, SceneEntry, SceneRegistry` — RetainedScene is referenced by full path at 1029 and SceneFilter is not imported here. The two stale computations differ in shape (presentation omits retained entries) — `stale_entries` must return both and the presentation must compare the same data. Methods go on storage::registry::SceneRegistry now (domain must not import storage per architecture_tests.rs:625-640, so a later move to domain/registry.rs means moving the type, not referencing it).

findings.title: Deck slot projection lives in the Live GTK page and is consumed by hotkeys and window code
findings.evidence: `live_scene_order`, `visible_scene_slots`, `scene_for_slot` (612-654) decide slot assignment from SceneInventory plus storage::registry::SceneRegistry. ui/hotkeys.rs:145 imports `pages::live::scene_for_slot`. inventory.rs:84-94 recomputes the same ordered-and-filtered list. Pure tests in live.rs:1307-1392.
findings.recommendation: Create `src/domain/deck.rs` with `DeckSlot { slot, scene: SceneId, favorite }`, `deck_projection(&SceneInventory, &SceneRegistrySnapshot) -> Vec<DeckSlot>` and `scene_for_slot`, taking the domain snapshot, not storage::SceneRegistry. Move the pure tests; re-export from live temporarily; migrate hotkeys.rs, live, inventory; delete re-export.
findings.risk: Slot assignment can diverge between Live cards, the hotkey dispatcher and Inventory order.
findings.verifier_note: Code confirmed at live.rs:612-654 and hotkeys.rs:145/161. Two errors: (a) inventory.rs:84-94 is NOT the same list — inventory shows all ordered+filtered scenes while live_scene_order filters to `is_live_switchable()` roles, so inventory must not switch to deck_projection. (b) domain/registry.rs::SceneRegistrySnapshot (lines 114-117) holds only `scenes: HashMap<SceneId, SceneMetadata>` and `graph_policy`; it has no saved order, filter or favourite data, while the projection needs `ordered_scene_ids`, `scene_matches_filter` (storage/registry/decks.rs:55) and `entry.favorite`. domain/ cannot import storage (architecture_tests.rs:625). Adjusted: introduce a domain `DeckInput { order: Vec<SceneId>, live_roles: HashMap<SceneId, SceneRole>, favorites: HashSet<SceneId>, filter matches }` (or extend SceneRegistrySnapshot with order/favorite) built by storage, then `domain/deck.rs` computes slots. Effort S -> M.

findings.title: The presentation-owner tuple is duplicated across pages, and Mixer detects changes with Debug-formatted strings
findings.evidence: (epoch, scope, registry_generation, registry_status, language) hand-assembled in live.rs:46-61, 78-85, 706-714; mixer.rs:31-45 (4-field MixerBinding); inventory.rs:60-66, 152-160; graph.rs:43-55; doctor.rs:36-48. 20 production occurrences of `show_registry.generation` in src/ui. Mixer signature is `format!("{:?}...")` (202-220) plus `controls_key` (370-376).
findings.recommendation: Add `#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] PresentationOwner { epoch, scope, registry_generation, registry_status, language }` with `AppState::presentation_owner()` in controller/state.rs, embed in every page presentation. Replace mixer strings with typed `MixerPresentation` and `MixerControlsKey`.
findings.risk: A new ownership dimension will be missed by one page, leaving stale controls bound to the wrong workspace.
findings.smell: Data Clumps / Duplicate Code / Primitive Obsession
findings.verifier_note: Verified: MixerBinding 4-tuple (no language) at mixer.rs:31-45; Debug-format signature 202-220; controls_key 370-376 (epoch, scope, language, scene ids — no registry generation/status); 20 production occurrences of show_registry.generation across src/ui (pages are 8 of them, rest in action_shortcuts, navigation, operator_picker, persist, quick_actions, deck_controls, window). Caution: the tuples are NOT identical — MixerBinding omits language, controls_key omits registry fields, doctor/graph keys omit registry_generation. A single PresentationOwner changes rebuild/request semantics at each site (e.g. adding language to MixerBinding resets request tracking on language change). Implementers must decide per site and add a test per page that pins which dimensions trigger rebuild.

findings.title: MixerPageHandle combines view handles, presenter signatures and the request-dedupe tracker; debug inspection lives in the page
findings.evidence: MixerPageHandle holds WeakRefs next to requested_scene, signature, binding, controls_signature (50-62). Request dedupe (1116-1194) decides AppCommand::RefreshMixerSceneAudio with state in a widget handle. emit_mixer_inspection reads `std::env::var(MIXER_INSPECT_ENV)` on every populate and uses eprintln! (947-952). ~110 lines of JSON formatting (955-1049).
findings.recommendation: Move tracker and decision into controller/state/mixer.rs: `MixerState::requested_scene` and `AppState::claim_mixer_scene_request(intent)`; port the 13 tests (1622-1786). Move inspection to mixer/inspection.rs; cache env flag in `static INSPECT: OnceLock<bool>`; emit through `tracing::info!(target: "scenedeck::mixer_inspect")` keeping the line format.
findings.risk: Dedupe state is lost whenever the page is rebuilt, which can cause duplicate OBS requests.
findings.verifier_note: Structure confirmed (handle fields 50-62; dedupe 1116-1194; env read every call 946; eprintln). Two corrections: (1) Risk overstated — duplicate OBS requests are already prevented by AppState status: `should_request_mixer_scene_audio` returns false for Loading/Loaded, and request_mixer_scene_audio sets `set_mixer_audio_loading` in AppState before dispatch; the page tracker only guards the Error+Automatic loop. (2) Do NOT switch to `tracing::info!`: docs/manual-test-plan.md:361-365 and 406-410 document capturing the raw structured lines from SCENEDECK_MIXER_INSPECT=1 on stderr; tracing adds prefixes and is subject to RUST_LOG filtering. Keep eprintln, cache the flag in OnceLock, move code to mixer/inspection.rs. Moving the tracker into controller/state/mixer.rs is fine (plain Option<String>, no GTK).

findings.title: mixer::populate is 204 lines, holds an AppState borrow across widget construction and signal wiring, and needs a manual drop(state)
findings.evidence: `let state = nav.state.borrow();` at 360 held through controls build (380-486); `drop(state)` at 528 before request_visible_mixer_scene_audio which borrow_muts (1150). Test at 1923 exists to catch that panic. Comment 356-359 calls the long borrow deliberate.
findings.recommendation: Compute a pure `enum MixerBody { NoScenes, MissingScene, Loading, Error, NeedsRequest, Loaded{..} }` inside one short `nav.read(...)`, render via controls::ensure and body::render, dispatch NeedsRequest after rendering outside any borrow.
findings.risk: Any new synchronous signal emission during build raises BorrowMutError.
findings.verifier_note: Verified populate at mixer.rs:355, borrow at 360 with deliberate comment 356-359, `drop(state)` at 528 before request_visible_mixer_scene_audio, which borrow_muts in request_mixer_scene_audio (set_mixer_audio_loading). Native test at 1923 exists. Recommendation is sound; note the long borrow was chosen to avoid cloning AppState — the MixerBody must borrow or clone only the visible inputs, not the whole state.

findings.title: Doctor and Graph duplicate the topology presentation key and the notice chain, cloning the whole graph and registry on every refresh
findings.evidence: Both stateful_page key closures build epoch, language, scene ids, scene_graph.edges.clone(), registry.snapshot(), show_registry.status.clone(), topology_status.clone() (doctor 33-49, graph 41-56); doctor adds obs-connected. Both chain topology_status.notice().or_else(registry_availability_message).
findings.recommendation: Add src/ui/pages/topology.rs with `TopologyPresentation { owner: PresentationOwner, topology_generation: u64, connected: bool }` (requires a generation counter on topology_status or scene_graph) and `topology_notice(nav)`.
findings.risk: Drift between the two pages; O(graph) clones per refresh while either page is mapped.
findings.verifier_note: Duplication confirmed (doctor.rs:33-49 vs graph.rs:41-56 nearly identical; notice chains doctor 119-124, graph 74-77). The generation-counter recommendation is risky: the current keys compare content (edges, registry.snapshot()), which catches registry edits that no generation counter tracks today (show_registry.generation is a workspace/registry-target binding, not an edit counter). Adjusted step 1: extract `fn topology_key(state:&AppState) -> TopologyKey` (same content comparison) and `topology_notice(nav)` into src/ui/pages/topology.rs; only replace content with generations after adding a counter bumped on every scene_graph/registry/topology mutation, with tests. stateful_page (ui/mod.rs:57-93) recomputes the key on every refresh, so the clone cost claim is right.

findings.title: Stream-health thresholds and severity policy are defined in the Stats page and duplicate domain/health.rs
findings.evidence: FPS_*/FRAME_TIME_*/DROPPED_*/CONGESTION_* constants (43-54); fps_target, frame_budget_ms, fps_severity, frame_time_severity, dropped_severity (852-899) return chart::Severity. domain/health.rs:27 defines SKIPPED_RATIO = 0.01 separately.
findings.recommendation: Create src/domain/stats/health.rs (or extend domain/health.rs): HealthLevel, StatsHealthPolicy, fps_level, frame_time_level, dropped_level, congestion_level, frame_budget_ms; health.rs::SKIPPED_RATIO references the same constant; `impl From<HealthLevel> for chart::Severity`; move tests 1074-1157.
findings.risk: Green gauge while an alert fires, or the reverse, after only one threshold is tuned.
findings.verifier_note: Constants and functions confirmed at stats.rs:43-54 and 852-899. The 'disagree' claim is mis-attributed: the stats gauge uses a cumulative ratio (`s.dropped_ratio()` / `output_skipped_ratio()`, stats.rs:413-416) while domain/health.rs:150-159 uses a per-interval delta between samples. They can disagree even with identical constants; a test asserting both share one constant proves little. Adjusted: move thresholds/severity into domain (e.g. domain/stats.rs or domain/health/thresholds.rs — domain/health/ dir already exists) as HealthLevel + From impl in chart.rs; share the 1% constant by name; document the cumulative-vs-windowed difference instead of claiming equivalence. fps_target currently takes &AppState; the domain version must take `Option<&StatsSample>` (domain/stats.rs:98).

findings.title: Per-frame tick callbacks on Live and a 100 ms poll for registry save status
findings.evidence: live.rs adds two add_tick_callback closures returning Continue forever, reading window height and toggling classes/spacing/margins/visibility/orientation every frame. inventory.rs:570 `glib::timeout_add_local(100ms, refresh)`, a new timer per non-incremental rebuild, running until WeakRefs die.

findings.title: The hotkey leader-timeout SpinRow writes config.json on every value-notify
findings.evidence: `timeout_row.connect_value_notify(move |row| { persist_config(&nav, |config| config.hotkeys.leader_timeout_ms = millis); refresh(); })`. Holding an arrow key issues one background write per step.
findings.recommendation: Update AppState immediately and debounce persistence with a 400 ms glib::timeout_add_local_once, or persist on focus-leave; optional ui::persist::DebouncedConfigWrite helper.
findings.risk: Write amplification and IO-lane backlog.
findings.verifier_note: persist_config (ui/persist.rs:463-470) routes through background_io::run_config_snapshot (background_io.rs:193-207), which coalesces: each call replaces `batch.latest` and only starts a worker if none is running. Rapid steps produce at most one in-flight write plus one pending latest snapshot, no backlog. The doc comment there says 'Admit a replaceable whole Config snapshot now, never via a debounce timer' — the proposed 400 ms debounce contradicts a deliberate design (Close/Quit must see pending intent). AppState is already updated synchronously inside persist_config. No change needed.
